title: Unmetabolized folic acid in plasma is associated with reduced natural killer cell cytotoxicity among postmenopausal women
authors: Troen AM, Mitchell B, Sorensen B, Wener MH, Johnston A, Wood B, et al.
population: Healthy, sedentary, overweight or obese postmenopausal women aged 50 to 75 years in the Seattle area, recruited in 1998 to 2000 for an exercise intervention trial, non-smoking and without hormone replacement therapy
funder: Supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health (R01 CA69334; T32 CA80416) and the U.S. Department of Agriculture cooperative research agreement 58-1950-4-401.
result: Unmetabolised folic acid was detected in 78% of fasting plasma samples. Natural killer cell cytotoxicity was about 23% lower in women with detectable folic acid (P = 0.04), with a stronger relation at age 60 years or over and with increasing concentrations (P for trend 0.002). Women with a folate-rich diet who also took folic acid supplements above 400 µg/day had lower NK cytotoxicity than those with a low-folate diet and no supplements (P = 0.02), whereas with a low-folate diet (below 233 µg/day) supplement users had greater cytotoxicity (P = 0.01).
